Tidy a survival model into a table of hazard ratios

tidy.survival_model.Rd

One row per exit type and covariate, with its hazard ratio, test and confidence interval. Call it as broom::tidy(fit).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'survival_model'
tidy(x, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

x

A survival_model from fit_survival_model().

conf.level

Number. The confidence level. Default 0.95.

...

Not used.

Value

A tibble with one row per exit type and term, and none if the model has no covariates:

exit_type

"retired" or "other".

term

The covariate as fixest names it: a category's column and level (e.g. genderM), or a numeric column's name.

covariate, level

The term split in two: the column (gender) and the category compared with the reference (M). level is NA for a numeric covariate.

estimate

The hazard ratio: e.g. 0.8 is a 20% lower chance of leaving in a given year than the reference category (or per unit of a numeric covariate).

std.error, statistic, p.value

On the log scale (see Details).

conf.low, conf.high

The confidence interval of the hazard ratio.

Details

estimate, conf.low and conf.high are exp() of the coefficient and its Wald interval; std.error, statistic (z) and p.value are for the log coefficient, as broom::tidy() gives them for survival::coxph(). The tenure band and year fixed effects (the baseline hazard) are left out: see fixest::fixef().

See also

fit_survival_model() for the model.

Examples

library(data.table)
contracts <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_contract)
personnel <- as.data.table(bra_hrmis_personnel)
tenure <- compute_tenure_panel(contracts)
personnel <- merge(personnel, tenure, by = c("personnel_id", "ref_date"), all.x = TRUE)

panel <- build_survival_panel(
  personnel, contracts,
  tenure_col = "tenure_years", salary_col = "gross_salary_lcu",
  status_col = "employment_status", covariate_cols = "gender"
)
fit <- fit_survival_model(panel, band_width = 5)
#> Warning: 54 person-intervals have a missing value in `tenure_years` or `gender` and are left out of the model.
broom::tidy(fit)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   exit_type term   covariate level estimate std.error statistic p.value conf.low
#>   <chr>     <chr>  <chr>     <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 retired   gende… gender    MASC…    0.718     0.130     -2.55  0.0107    0.557
#> 2 other     gende… gender    MASC…    0.893     0.113     -1.01  0.315     0.716
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: conf.high <dbl>
